ai.title: SDK applies Zod schema to custom tool input
ai.summary: SDK custom tool handlers now receive validated `Output` types instead of raw `Input`, enforced via `zodSchema.parse` in `sdk/src/client.ts`. `sdk/src/custom-tool.ts` updates `handler` signatures to match this transformation. `backend/src/tools/tool-executor.ts` ensures `endsAgentStepParam` is stripped from a cloned input object before parsing, preventing mutation issues.

eli5.text: When you give a tool to the assistant, the system now checks that the input you provide matches the expected format before the tool runs, instead of just passing your input straight through unchanged. If your input had any extra, internal-only fields attached to it, those are now removed before the check happens, so your tool receives clean, properly shaped data. Tools that were already working will receive the same practical data as before, just with a safety check applied first; any tool whose inputs didn't actually match its expected format would now fail instead of silently receiving something unexpected. This is live and applies to anyone building or using custom tools with the SDK today.

ai.title: Fix typecheck for dynamic-agent-template
ai.summary: Updated type definition in common/src/types/__tests__/dynamic-agent-template.test.ts to allow string literals alongside published tools. The toolNames type now includes (string & {}) union to resolve typecheck errors. This ensures compatibility with dynamic agent template definitions.

eli5.text: The system had a small mismatch in how it checked agent template definitions, causing type validation to fail when a tool name was a plain string rather than a specifically published tool. This fix broadens the accepted tool name type so that dynamic agent templates can include arbitrary string tool names alongside the known published tools. Who it affects: The developer-facing type checker and test suite for agent template definitions. End-users of the platform are not directly affected by this change. What you would notice: If you looked at the test file or ran type checking, the type checker no longer errors on dynamic agent templates that declare tool names as plain strings. The change is in place and resolves a previously failing validation during development.

ai.title: Add deep-thinking agent orchestration system
ai.summary: New multi-agent framework in `.agents/deep-thinking/` spawns parallel sub-agents (GPT-5, Sonnet, Gemini) to synthesize complex analysis. `deepest-thinker.ts` decomposes problems into four aspects, delegating to `deep-thinker.ts`, which coordinates three specialized thinkers to merge perspectives. The `agent-builder.ts` removes verbose step-by-step prompting, relying on atomic tool usage and default end_turn behavior. This structure enables recursive, multi-model reasoning for high-complexity tasks.

eli5.text: The system added a new way for multiple AI helpers to team up and think through tough problems together. Instead of one assistant tackling a complex question alone, it can now break the problem into parts and send different specialized helpers (each tuned for deep, balanced, or creative thinking) to work on pieces in parallel, then stitch their answers back together. If you look closely, you'd see fewer wordy step-by-step instructions baked into how these helpers are built, replaced by a leaner setup that lets each helper focus on its one job before passing results along. This is live now for internal use, so the assistant can quietly summon these coordinated helper teams whenever a question is too big for a single pass.
